tasks.short: Explain site costs and commitments and advise on the next forecast.

today.trigger: A forecast update, operational change or management question requires a financial assessment.
steps: Pull actual costs and revenues from AFAS and Power BI.
Collect commitments, staffing assumptions and operational explanations from site managers.
Reconcile the figures and build revenue and expense projections in Excel.
Discuss the assumptions with FP&A and recommend a course of action.
drudgery: Copying figures between extracts and forecast workbooks
Checking whether commitments are already included
today.time_sinks: Reconciling different reporting dates and chasing explanations for changes in transport, warehouse and flex labour costs.

lenses.faster: On an illustrative four-hour analysis, linked extracts and a source-backed draft remove two hours of assembly; assumption checks and discussion still take two hours.
lenses.autonomous: An approved forecast snapshot starts the workflow, which calculates comparisons and drafts an explanation from supplied evidence. The accountant approves assumptions and advice before anything enters the forecast.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo managers a weekly financial assessment of proposed overtime and flex staffing changes. Demand would grow if each assessment became cheaper and arrived before the staffing decision.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the same spreadsheets; the accountant gets more time to understand why a site is missing its margin.
lenses.options: Compare volume growth, agency rate increases and overtime alternatives with the same capacity assumptions. Different cash and margin outcomes can change the staffing recommendation.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts towards challenging forecast drivers with site managers, with delegated authority to return unsupported assumptions for revision. The work becomes more expert because operational judgement matters more than spreadsheet assembly.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's first-pass site cost-driver analysis after learning forecast ownership, operational volume measures and scenario modelling.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant distinguishes a temporary timing issue from a lasting operational problem and challenges assumptions that look plausible in the data but fail on the warehouse floor.
tasks.pattern_why: A fixed extraction and calculation workflow can feed one model call that drafts a checkable explanation; open-ended agent navigation is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: FP&A releases a versioned forecast input pack or requests a defined site assessment.
steps: Load the approved AFAS extract, forecast version and dated commitment schedule.
Calculate site trends and scenarios using controlled formulas.
Draft an explanation linking each material statement to a figure or manager-supplied assumption.
Have the accountant resolve gaps and approve the analysis before FP&A incorporates it.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves assumptions and advice; FP&A and budget owners retain authority over the forecast.
data_needed: Actuals by site, account and period
Approved forecast drivers and operational volumes
Open commitments with dates and accounting treatment
Versioned site-manager explanations
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint analysis folder containing source versions, formulas, cited draft, reviewer changes and approval.

evidence.claim: Accounting benchmarks show that judgement and multi-step reasoning remain failure points, supporting explicit review of forecast assumptions.
Controlled calculations followed by source-backed narrative drafting are feasible, but Noordhaven's integration and savings require a pilot.

risks: The nightly Power BI extract can omit recent transactions or commitments.
Scenarios may double-count flex costs or treat correlations as cost drivers.
A fluent explanation may hide an unsupported operational assumption.
research_questions: Can actuals, commitments and forecast drivers be joined reliably by site and reporting date?
Which operational measures explain transport and warehouse costs well enough to support scenarios?
Does a pilot halve total preparation time while preserving forecast accuracy and review quality?

tasks.short: Find control failures, duplicate spending and suspicious transactions across the three sites.

today.trigger: A scheduled control review, unusual transaction or management concern requires investigation.
steps: Collect ledger, supplier, payment and agency invoice records.
Compare transactions and approvals against documented control requirements.
Inspect exceptions and obtain supporting documents or explanations.
Document substantiated findings and agree corrective action with the Controller.
today.time_sinks: Separating genuine exceptions from normal recurring charges and obtaining reliable evidence of approvals and master-data changes.

lenses.faster: On an illustrative five-hour review, automated matching and evidence assembly remove three hours; investigating exceptions and agreeing findings still take two hours.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled transaction extract starts duplicate, approval and supplier-bank-change tests without the accountant. The accountant investigates exceptions before any finding, accusation or corrective action is recorded as substantiated.
lenses.ambitious: Decision made more often: decide each working day which payment-control exceptions need investigation before the next payment batch. Demand would grow as cheaper screening makes earlier intervention practical.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss comparing invoice numbers row by row; the accountant gets more time to establish causes and fix recurring weaknesses.
lenses.options: Compare duplicate-detection thresholds and approval-control designs against historical transactions. The resulting false-positive and missed-exception rates change which controls are adopted.
lenses.altitude: The week centres on exception investigation and control improvement, with delegated authority to escalate unresolved exceptions to the payment approver. The role becomes more expert in evidence assessment and control design.
reach: Absorb the Controller's routine transaction-control testing after learning evidence standards, segregation of duties and escalation procedures.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant evaluates explanations, distinguishes error from suspected misconduct and conducts sensitive conversations without treating an automated flag as proof.
tasks.pattern_why: Duplicate, approval and bank-change tests can be expressed as explicit rules and run repeatedly without a model.

in_practice.trigger: A daily AFAS extract and payment-batch file become available.
steps: Validate extract completeness and reconcile transaction totals to AFAS.
Run approved duplicate, approval, segregation-of-duties and IBAN-change tests.
Create exception records with rule identifiers and supporting transaction references.
Have the accountant investigate exceptions and escalate substantiated findings to the Controller.
in_practice.human_gate: Tests run automatically; a human determines the finding, any payment hold and corrective action under existing authority.
data_needed: Invoice and payment identifiers, amounts and dates
Supplier master-data changes and verification records
Approval histories and user-role assignments
Agency invoices and approved hours
Documented control rules and exceptions
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint control register with extract totals, rule versions, exception evidence, investigator decisions and closure.

evidence.claim: Rules-based transaction checks can identify potential duplicates and control exceptions; they cannot establish fraudulent intent.
Accounting workpapers can become unreliable when AI introduces assumptions that cannot be reconstructed, supporting explicit evidence and rule logs.

risks: Incomplete approval or master-data histories can make apparent control coverage misleading.
Repeated legitimate charges can create excessive false positives.
Employee-linked exception data requires restricted access and proportionate retention under AVG/GDPR; proposed monitoring changes need assessment with HR and the OR.
research_questions: Does AFAS expose complete approval, user-role and supplier-change histories?
Which tests would have detected known past errors without overwhelming the accountant?
Can every exception be reconstructed from retained source evidence?
Would the proposed use constitute employee monitoring requiring OR involvement?

tasks.short: Maintain site budgets and explain actual spending against the approved plan.

today.trigger: A monthly close, budget round or revised operating plan requires an updated comparison.
steps: Retrieve approved budgets and actual costs by site and account.
Align account mappings, reporting periods and budget versions.
Calculate variances and collect explanations from budget owners.
Prepare the comparison report and agree corrections with FP&A.
drudgery: Repairing workbook links and account mappings
today.time_sinks: Resolving budget-version differences and determining whether overspend reflects timing, volume, rates or an accounting error.

lenses.faster: On an illustrative four-hour reporting cycle, automated comparisons and drafted explanations remove 156 minutes; checking material variances and agreeing changes still take 84 minutes.
lenses.autonomous: An approved monthly actuals snapshot starts the comparison and commentary draft. The accountant approves explanations and corrections, while budget owners approve changes to their budgets.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give each site manager a weekly warning of likely month-end budget breaches with the remaining spending headroom. Demand would grow if producing a reliable warning became cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss repairing spreadsheets; the accountant gets more time to help managers act on avoidable overspending.
lenses.options: Compare the original budget, a volume-adjusted budget and a revised spending plan. These alternatives distinguish operational inefficiency from extra workload and can change the response.
lenses.altitude: The week moves towards resolving material variances and advising budget owners, with delegated authority to require evidence before accepting an explanation. The job becomes more expert in cost behaviour and accounting cut-off.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's recurring budget-versus-actual pack after learning budget governance and the distinction between accounting corrections and forecast revisions.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant decides whether a variance reflects a real operating issue, a budget assumption or a posting error, and challenges convenient explanations.
tasks.pattern_why: Controlled formulas produce the comparison; one model call turns supplied figures and owner comments into a reviewable variance narrative.

in_practice.trigger: The Controller releases a reconciled actuals snapshot and FP&A identifies the approved budget version.
steps: Validate mappings and reconcile actuals to the general ledger.
Calculate amount, percentage and approved volume-adjusted variances.
Draft commentary using transaction evidence and attributed budget-owner comments.
Have the accountant approve the report and route proposed budget changes to their owners.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs off the comparison and explanations; budget approval rights remain with designated owners.
data_needed: Approved budgets with version and owner
Actuals by site, account and period
Account-to-budget mappings
Approved operational volume drivers
Budget-owner explanations and supporting documents
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint budget-report library retaining source versions, reconciliation totals, commentary edits and approvals.

evidence.claim: Budget comparisons can use deterministic calculations, with language models drafting explanations from supplied evidence.
A field study reported faster closes among AI-using accountants, but its results do not establish Noordhaven's task-level savings.

risks: An unapproved budget version can produce a convincing but invalid comparison.
Missing accruals or stale extracts can create false spending headroom.
A model may invent a causal explanation when only a numerical variance is known.
research_questions: Is there one approved budget source with reliable version control and ownership?
Which sites have sufficiently reliable volume data for a volume-adjusted comparison?
How much commentary can be supported directly by evidence rather than inferred?
Does the pilot reduce total reporting time without increasing corrections after publication?

tasks.short: Check Dutch payroll premiums, liabilities and CAO treatment against personnel records.

today.trigger: A payroll cycle, year-end review or premium change requires an independent accounting check.
steps: Obtain payroll totals and the personnel fields needed for the selected checks.
Compare payroll setup with applicable Dutch premium, tax and CAO requirements.
Reconcile payroll liabilities and postings to AFAS general-ledger balances.
Investigate exceptions with Payroll and HR and document corrections.
systems: AFAS Profit HR, payroll and general ledger
drudgery: Comparing contract attributes with payroll settings
Matching payroll totals to ledger liabilities
today.time_sinks: Resolving contract classifications, effective dates and differences between employees and agency workers.

lenses.faster: On an illustrative four-hour payroll review, automatic reconciliations and approved rule tests remove 132 minutes; investigating exceptions and agreeing corrections still take 108 minutes.
lenses.autonomous: A completed payroll calculation starts approved premium and liability tests. Only exceptions need accountant review, and Payroll approves every resulting payroll correction or filing change.
lenses.ambitious: Decision made more often: assess the financial exposure from contract and premium exceptions before each payroll finalisation. Demand would grow if this check became cheap enough to run reliably every cycle.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss repetitive payroll-to-ledger matching; the accountant gets more time to resolve recurring classification and liability problems with Payroll.
lenses.options: Compare the cost and effective date of legally valid correction routes with Payroll, including correction now or through an authorised later adjustment. Cash, employee impact and filing consequences can change the chosen route.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts towards payroll assurance, with delegated authority to require an unresolved material exception to be escalated before payroll sign-off. The work becomes more expert in Dutch payroll accounting and effective-dated rules.
reach: Absorb the Payroll Specialist's routine payroll-to-ledger reconciliation and premium-exception preparation after learning Awf, Whk, Zvw, pension and relevant CAO treatment.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant and Payroll Specialist interpret ambiguous contract facts, validate Dutch legal treatment and decide how to correct errors affecting employees.
tasks.pattern_why: Reconciliations and approved, effective-dated payroll checks are repeatable rules; a model is unnecessary for their execution.

in_practice.trigger: Payroll marks a calculation complete and makes a restricted review extract available.
steps: Load only required contract attributes, payroll components, applicable rates and ledger totals.
Run approved premium, liability, effective-date and CAO configuration checks.
Reconcile payroll postings and liabilities to AFAS and produce an exception list.
Have the accountant investigate with Payroll, which authorises corrections and confirms resolution.
in_practice.human_gate: Automated checks create exceptions only; Payroll retains payroll and tax-filing authority, with HR resolving contract facts.
data_needed: Pseudonymised employee identifiers and necessary contract attributes
Payroll components, bases and calculated premiums
Approved current Dutch rates and employer-specific premium notices
Relevant CAO and pension configuration
Payroll journal and liability balances
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted payroll-control register recording source versions, rule versions, totals, exception decisions and Payroll approval.

evidence.claim: This US-worded task should be implemented as checks of Noordhaven's Dutch payroll premiums, liabilities and employment arrangements.
Effective-dated deterministic rules can automate payroll reconciliations and flag classification exceptions, subject to validated local configuration.

risks: Incorrect or outdated premium rules can systematically misstate liabilities.
Applying employee payroll rules to agency workers can assign obligations to the wrong employer.
Payroll data is sensitive under AVG/GDPR; medical details and Wet verbetering poortwachter case files are unnecessary for these checks.
Extending checks into employee scoring or employment decisions would require a separate legal and EU AI Act assessment.
research_questions: Which payroll errors recur, and can approved rules detect them before finalisation?
Are contract changes and employer-specific premium notices complete and effective-dated?
Can the review work without medical information or unnecessary personal data?
Are obligations for Noordhaven employees and agency workers clearly separated?

tasks.short: Advise HR and Finance on employment costs, benefits and accounting-system choices.

today.trigger: HR, the Finance Director or a project owner asks for advice on a proposed policy or system change.
steps: Clarify the decision, affected groups and financial constraints.
Collect policy, CAO, tax and system information with the relevant specialists.
Calculate costs and compare feasible alternatives.
Discuss trade-offs and document advice for the accountable decision-maker.
drudgery: Finding the current policy and contract template
today.time_sinks: Clarifying the actual decision and reconciling Finance, HR and operational priorities.

lenses.faster: On an illustrative two-hour advice request, document retrieval and comparison drafting remove 30 minutes; validating treatment and discussing trade-offs still take 90 minutes.
lenses.autonomous: A defined advice request starts assisted retrieval and scenario preparation under the accountant's direction. The accountant checks the advice and the relevant HR or Finance owner makes the decision.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give the warehouse L&D team a financial assessment of alternative certificate-renewal schedules, including training cost and shift-cover cost. Demand would grow if smaller scheduling changes could receive affordable advice.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching policy folders; the accountant gets more time to understand stakeholder needs and explain difficult trade-offs.
lenses.options: Compare eligible benefit designs or phased system-rollout choices using cost, employee impact and implementation effort. Several viable alternatives can reveal a better decision than the requester's first proposal.
lenses.altitude: The week includes more cross-functional advisory work, with delegated authority to validate financial assumptions before a proposal reaches Finance leadership. The role becomes more expert, while HR retains employment-policy decisions.
reach: Absorb the Compensation and Benefits Specialist's first-pass costing of policy alternatives after learning CAO boundaries, payroll-tax treatment and benefit eligibility.
Absorb the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's finance-impact assessment for AFAS changes after learning interface design and access controls.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant discovers what stakeholders are really trying to achieve, recognises sensitive employee consequences and knows when a Dutch tax or employment specialist is needed.
tasks.pattern_why: The request and trade-offs require human-led conversation; AI can retrieve material and prepare alternatives within that discussion.

in_practice.trigger: An internal owner submits a defined policy, benefit or system decision for financial advice.
steps: Agree the decision scope, affected groups, constraints and accountable owner.
Retrieve approved documents and prepare cost calculations using aggregated data where possible.
Use the assistant to draft alternatives, assumptions and questions for HR, Payroll or a tax specialist.
Have the accountant validate the analysis and discuss advice with the decision-maker.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant owns the advice; HR, Payroll and Finance approve matters within their authority, including required OR consultation or consent procedures.
data_needed: The decision brief and affected employee groups
Current CAOs, policies and eligibility rules
Aggregated employment costs and relevant tax assumptions
System requirements, costs and implementation constraints
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint decision file containing assumptions, source documents, reviewed options and the owner's recorded decision.

evidence.claim: Accounting benchmark work explicitly leaves out client communication, asking the right questions and tacit context, which are central to this advisory task.
AFAS Jonas provides contextual tax assistance in supported returns and explicitly leaves checking responsibility with the user; this does not establish general HR-advice capability.

risks: Advice based on an outdated CAO or policy can misstate eligibility or costs.
A model may overstate tax certainty or miss the need for specialist advice.
Individual employment data may be disclosed unnecessarily when group-level figures would suffice.
research_questions: Which recurring advice requests consume enough preparation time to justify a reusable workflow?
Can current CAOs, policies and tax assumptions be retrieved with clear dates and ownership?
Do reviewed alternatives change decisions, or merely make the briefing faster?
Which proposals require HR, external tax advice or formal OR involvement?

tasks.short: Check finance and payroll system changes before they go live.

today.trigger: A proposed AFAS configuration, interface or reporting change reaches the pre-release review stage.
steps: Read requirements and identify accounting and control risks.
Prepare representative test cases and expected financial results.
Run tests in a separate environment and reconcile resulting records.
Investigate failures and report release conditions to the project owner.
systems: AFAS Profit test environment, if available
drudgery: Writing similar test cases for each change
Comparing expected and actual output manually
today.time_sinks: Converting vague requirements into testable financial outcomes and reproducing failures across interfaces.

lenses.faster: On an illustrative eight-hour review, assisted test design and automated comparisons remove 2.8 hours; risk assessment, failure investigation and sign-off work still take 5.2 hours.
lenses.autonomous: A versioned change request prompts test-case drafting, and approved tests can execute in a separate environment. The accountant judges coverage and unresolved failures before recommending release.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give HRIS and Finance project owners a financial-control impact assessment before small AFAS changes are built. Demand would grow if this assessment became cheap enough for minor changes.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss collecting repetitive test evidence; the accountant gets more time to find the failure that would otherwise surface during payroll or close.
lenses.options: Compare rollout with a temporary reconciliation, a parallel run or an interface redesign. The residual risks and operational workload can change the release approach.
lenses.altitude: The week includes earlier design reviews and release-risk decisions, with delegated authority to withhold finance-control sign-off when agreed criteria fail. The job becomes more expert in systems and accounting controls.
reach: Absorb the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's finance-side acceptance testing after learning AFAS configuration, interface behaviour and test-data management.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant spots missing requirements, chooses realistic failure cases and decides whether a technically passing change preserves the intended accounting and controls.
tasks.pattern_why: Risk assessment and test coverage remain human-led; assisted drafting and deterministic test execution support that judgement.

in_practice.trigger: A project owner submits a versioned change specification for finance-control review.
steps: Map requirements to affected postings, reconciliations, approvals and access rights.
Draft normal, boundary and failure tests with independently checked expected results.
Run approved tests against synthetic or appropriately masked data in a separate environment.
Review failures and missing coverage, then record the accountant's release recommendation.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves coverage and finance-control sign-off; the designated change owner authorises deployment.
data_needed: Versioned requirements and configuration changes
Interface specifications and account mappings
Approved control requirements
Synthetic or masked test records
Independently established expected accounting results
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint change-review file linking requirements, test versions, expected and actual results, defects and sign-offs.

evidence.claim: AI can assist test drafting and comparison-script creation, but safe execution depends on available test environments and independently validated expected results.
Documented accounting benchmarks expose multi-step reasoning failures, so generated tests and their expected outcomes need independent review.

risks: Tests generated from the same mistaken interpretation as the implementation can falsely pass.
A test environment may differ materially from production.
Real payroll or personnel data can enter development tools without adequate protection.
Passing transaction tests may conceal missing approval or access-control tests.
research_questions: Is a separate AFAS test environment available with representative interfaces and access roles?
Can expected postings and control outcomes be established independently of generated tests?
Which previous release defects would the proposed test pack have caught?
Does evidence preparation save time after accounting for test review and maintenance?

tasks.short: Explain asset use and audit findings to management and recommend practical changes.

today.trigger: A management review, completed control review or concern about asset costs requires a report.
steps: Collect asset costs, available utilisation records and verified audit findings.
Reconcile financial figures and distinguish confirmed findings from open questions.
Develop recommendations with operational owners.
Present the report and agree actions, owners and follow-up dates.
drudgery: Updating action tables from meeting notes
today.time_sinks: Obtaining comparable utilisation measures and turning financial findings into changes site managers can implement.

lenses.faster: On an illustrative four-hour report, reconciled tables and a source-linked narrative remove 108 minutes; checking recommendations and discussing actions still take 132 minutes.
lenses.autonomous: A completed review or approved reporting snapshot starts report drafting and action-list preparation. The accountant approves findings and recommendations before management receives them.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give site managers a quarterly review of whether to repair, redeploy or replace underused handling equipment. Demand would grow if comparable evidence became cheaper to assemble.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding presentation tables; the accountant gets more time to help managers choose and follow through on useful changes.
lenses.options: Compare repair, lease, replacement and transfer between sites using cash cost, utilisation and service constraints. Several options can change the recommendation from buying equipment to redeploying it.
lenses.altitude: The week moves towards management discussions and action follow-up, with delegated authority to challenge unsupported closure of audit actions. The role becomes more expert in operational economics and evidence-based recommendations.
reach: Absorb the Controller's preparation of the audit-action management pack after learning finding severity, action governance and escalation.
Absorb the FP&A Analyst's initial equipment-option appraisal after learning investment evaluation and operational capacity constraints.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant judges whether a recommendation is workable, handles disagreement about findings and communicates uncertainty without weakening accountability.
tasks.pattern_why: A fixed pack of reconciled figures and approved findings supports one checkable report draft; recommendation approval stays with the accountant.

in_practice.trigger: The accountant marks review findings ready or the Controller releases an approved reporting snapshot.
steps: Reconcile asset values and costs to AFAS and validate available utilisation measures.
Calculate approved comparisons and separate confirmed findings from unresolved questions.
Draft a report with evidence references, feasible options and proposed action owners.
Have the accountant validate recommendations and present the approved report for management decisions.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves the report; operational owners validate feasibility and management authorises spending or operational changes.
data_needed: Asset register, depreciation, lease and maintenance costs
Available operating hours, downtime and capacity measures
Verified audit findings and supporting evidence
Option costs and operational constraints
Action owners, due dates and closure evidence
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint management-report library and action register retaining source versions, reviewed recommendations, decisions and closure evidence.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft management narratives from structured figures and verified findings; the proposed asset appraisal depends on operational data not established in the supplied stack.
Strong performance on bounded accounting scenarios does not cover communication, asking questions or tacit context needed for management recommendations.

risks: Book value and depreciation are poor substitutes for actual utilisation.
Inconsistent site measures can create misleading asset comparisons.
A drafted recommendation can omit safety, peak-capacity or maintenance constraints.
Actions may be marked complete without evidence that the underlying control improved.
research_questions: Are comparable equipment utilisation and downtime records available across the three sites?
Can the report link every material finding and recommendation to retained evidence?
Do managers act on the options, and can benefits be checked after implementation?
Does drafting save time once recommendation review and operational consultation are included?

role.altitude: The accountant becomes the person who assures that financial explanations, payroll reconciliations and control findings are supported before they reach decision-makers. With explicit delegation from the Controller, the role can require reconciliations, return unsupported assumptions and withhold finance-control sign-off against agreed criteria.
reach: FP&A Analyst: recurring site variance packs and first-pass operational scenarios, after learning forecast governance and cost drivers.
Controller: routine transaction-control testing and audit-action reporting, after learning evidence standards and escalation.
Payroll Specialist: payroll-to-ledger reconciliation and approved premium checks, after learning Dutch payroll rules and CAO treatment.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: finance-side acceptance testing for AFAS changes, after learning interfaces, permissions and test-data management.
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks total 217.8 hours per accountant annually, about 14% of the supplied role-time basis. The proposed savings total about 107.5 hours per accountant, or 215 hours across two FTE, worth roughly EUR 15,000 of annual capacity at EUR 70/hour before setup and maintenance; all timings are illustrative estimates including human review, not measured savings or cash reductions.
skills_to_grow: AFAS extraction, data lineage and reconciliation design
SQL or Power Query and maintainable deterministic control tests
Dutch payroll, CAO and tax interpretation within clear specialist boundaries
Operational cost drivers and scenario evaluation
Evidence-based AI review and detection of unsupported assumptions
AVG/GDPR access controls, proportionate data use and OR consultation requirements
Test design, change assurance and clear communication with site managers
role.ambitious_version: Provide a regular financial assurance and decision-support service to all three sites: detect transaction and payroll exceptions before sign-off, explain emerging cost pressures and assess operational options before money is committed. Expand only where source quality and reviewed outcomes hold up, measuring days to close, forecast accuracy and audit adjustments alongside the preparation time saved.
